TraitDescription.Aetherfont: Options with the aetherfont trait pertain to a creature's aetherfont, or manatype. These options determine or unlock new ways for how a creature can use ether, which can include Aetherfont actions, archetypes, and their spells, all of which use ether.
TraitDescription.Aelkhazak: A creature with this trait is a member of the aelkhazak ancestry. These snake-like creatures come from aquatic environments, but are capable of inhabiting land.
TraitDescription.Anima: An option with the Anima trait relates to the natural power inherrent in the soul or a similar magical force that animates a nonliving creature such as a construct or undead. Anima spells or abilities come naturally to some creatures, while others either create facsimiles or borrow it from these creatures. They are almost always affiliated with the origin creature's family.
TraitDescription.Artifex: This indicates abilities from the Artifex class.
TraitDescription.Ardorean: An option with this trait indicates a high-powered variant of an existing Pathfinder option, or contains an adjustment that makes it more powerful than its original counterpart.
TraitDescription.Ascended: Options with this trait grant or utilize ascendancy. A creature with the ascended trait has exceeded their natural limitations, either in mind, body or soul. They are more powerful than typical creatures of their level. Feats and spells with this trait can only be taken by characters who have gained ascendency.
TraitDescription.Aspektus: An item with the aspektus trait has benefited from aspektus enchanting. Its power has been heightened from its original form.
TraitDescription.Astral: Effects with the Astral trait are tied to the mana forces of the astral planes. They often have stronger effects on telluric creatures. Creatures with this trait are tied to the workings of the astral planes and often have weakness to telluric.
TraitDescription.Agamidan: A creature with this trait is a member of the agamidan ancestry. These repitillian humanoids have existed in Ardor for millenia, hailing from the desert lands of Eirlangga.
TraitDescription.Avekiri: A creature with this trait is a member of the avekiri ancestry. The avian humanoids reside in mountainous or tree-top terrains typically, and their voices are said to be that of divinity.
TraitDescription.AzophFer: A creature with this trait is a member of the azoph-fer ancestry. They were created by Azoph-met, an ancient deity from the land of Zaho. They are strongly tied to him, but many strive for their own ends.
TraitDescription.Blood: A spell with this trait utilizes or is dependent on blood, either on the caster or the target's part. It is ineffective on creatures without some form of lifeblood, but expert practitioners are said to be able to bypass this limitation.
TraitDescription.CazicFer: A creature with this trait bears a cazic-fer heritage. Their physical and spiritual selves bear fiendish influences of one of the many children of Bapho-met.
TraitDescription.Catalogue: Items with the catalogue trait are service items, typically books, journals, manuscripts, recipes or blueprints that are meant to supplement or improve the wares or services of craftsmen or merchants. By default, they will specify what type of equipment they can provide, either with specific items or a general item level.
TraitDescription.Catalyze: Actions with the catalyze trait indicate an alternate effect when activating an ephemeral catalyst to change a spell about to be cast. When you Activate the catalyst through the action, you use the action’s listed changes to the spell rather than the ephemeral catalyst’s regular effects. If a number follows the Catalyze trait, you add the number of actions required to activating the Ephemeral Catalyst. The action might also list additional effects you can choose to add if have the Enhanced Catalyst or Visionary Catalyst feature.
TraitDescription.Catalyze1: Actions with the catalyze trait indicate an alternate effect when activating an ephemeral catalyst to change a spell about to be cast. When you Activate the catalyst through the action, you use the action’s listed changes to the spell rather than the ephemeral catalyst’s regular effects. If a number follows the Catalyze trait, you add the number of actions required to activating the Ephemeral Catalyst. The action might also list additional effects you can choose to add if have the Enhanced Catalyst or Visionary Catalyst feature.
TraitDescription.Chaos: Effects with the Chaos trait are tied to the universal concepts of anarchy, disrupting order and fate. They often have stronger effects on axiomatic creatures. Creatures with this trait are emblematic of anarchic forces and often have weakness to order.
TraitDescription.Chimerian: This indicates abilities from the Chimerian class.
TraitDescription.Charge: This indicates an Arcblade ability that requires its user to be in a state of heightened power, such as when they have the Panache for Swashbucklers or are channeling elements like a Kineticist.
TraitDescription.Combo: A weapon with the Combo trait has latent power or a mechanism to deal additional damage of the type listed in the trait. After a successful strike with the weapon, the next Strike they make before the end of their next turn gains the versatile damage trait of that type.
TraitDescription.Constellation: An option with the Constellation trait borrows power from the constellations in the sky, which reflect the facets of creation and what it stands for. Typically, only asters, practitioners of somnistry, are able to select options with this trait.
TraitDescription.Covenant: An option with the Covenant trait borrows power from the covenants inscribed into the universe's tapestry in the void of oblivion. Only those who can tap into or have been sworn into the covenants can access its powers and select options with this trait.
TraitDescription.Defend: An action with the Defend trait indicates abilities featuring a temporary act of defense. This typically comes in the form of a single action conferring a short-term circumstance bonus to AC or saving throw that lasts no more than until the start of the next turn of the character that used it. When an effect or another action calls for use of a Defend action or spell, you can take any Defend ability you have access unless it explicitly specifies that is the only action you can take.
TraitDescription.Dervish: This indicates abilities from the Dervish class.
TraitDescription.Discharge: This indicates an Arcblade ability that expends its user's state of heightened power. It gains the same trait as the class feature that expends this state, such as the Finisher trait for Swashbucklers or the Overflow trait for Kineticists.
TraitDescription.Diviner: This indicates abilities from the Diviner class.
TraitDescription.Draich: A creature with this trait bears a draich heritage. They bear draconic features gifted by a draichsar benefactor.
TraitDescription.Drachiri: Drachiri are draconic creatures of ether, empowered with the full array of telluric might and magic. Their family includes true drachiri and any of their magically created descendants. An option with this trait signifies that a drachiri benefactor's influence can change its effect, if the creature possesses one.
TraitDescription.Draichsar: A creature with this trait is a member of the draichsar ancestry. Creatures created in the image of the drachiri, they are humanoids with dragonlike wings and find their way in a life after the empire that created them.
TraitDescription.Empty: A creature with the Empty trait cannot cast spells or use actions that imply the use of ether, such as magic or feats of supernatural power.
TraitDescription.Engram: An item or feat with the Engram trait indicates that it has or adds an Ingrave activation to sygican technology, and thus it requires one to be using sygican equipment to make use of, unless indicated otherwise.
TraitDescription.Ether: An option with the ether trait relates to the telluric source of magic of the same name. Creatures in Ardor and Espiria require the use of ether for magical effects, such as spellcasting or actions dependent on the use of magic. Creatures who cannot use ether, such as Empty, cannot select these options. Most options with the Mana trait are replaced with the Ether trait if a creature of the Telluric planes gain access to it.
TraitDescription.Facet: A facet is a concept or idea given form, born out of imagination. It bears tangible form when in the astral planes. Denizens of the primal planes and asters in the astral planes can make use of facets in ways unique to each of them.
TraitDescription.Gangor: A creature with this trait is a member of the gangor ancestry. These diverse marsupial humanoids hail from the lands of Garrunga, able to easily commune with the spiritual planes and wield magic in a measured way as to not upset the balance of the world.
TraitDescription.Housing: Items with the housing trait are equipment that upgrades a residence. Each type of housing can hold a number of upgrades of different types.
TraitDescription.Launching: A weapon with the launching trait launches thrown weapons as projectiles. A launching weapon typically lists what thrown weapons it can take and launch, and its wielder can reload the weapon with a thrown weapon with one hand, and launch it through its mechanism with one or both hands afterward when they make a Strike. When launched, the throwing weapon acts as if you have thrown it with a strength modifier equal to what is listed on the trait, with a throwing range listed on the launching weapon. Runes on the Launching weapon that can apply to the thrown weapon will apply to the attack, overwriting any runes on the thrown weapon.
TraitDescription.Loupain: A creature with this trait is a member of the loupain ancestry. These canines are equally capable of moving with their hind legs and four legs both, and possess a strong sense of camraderie and survival instincts.
TraitDescription.Lucid: Actions with the lucid trait are those that are taken by figmentary creatures, typically those aligned or temporarily passing through the astral planes. A creature can only take one Lucid action each turn.
TraitDescription.Lyncan: A creature with this trait is a member of the lyncan ancestry. These magically infused feline humanoids are said to have been created through a world-wide cascade of transformative magic on Ardor's feline animals, and are always trying to find their place in the world that perceives them in wildly different ways.
TraitDescription.Mana: An option with the Mana trait relates to the astral powers of creation or oblivion prevalent in the astral planes. Typically, denizens of the astral planes have natural access to Mana, and it is their equivalent of Ether. Most options with the Ether trait are replaced with the Mana trait for these denizens if they gain access to it.
TraitDescription.Marine: A weapon with the Marine trait functions well in aquatic environments. It ignores typical limitations of attacking in water for weapons of its kind or damage types. At a GM's discretion, this can apply to other places where gravity or pressure is different, as well.
TraitDescription.Meal: Items with the meal trait are consumables that are crafted with Cooking Lore or Survival. They confer benefits that grant item bonuses, or increase existing item bonuses. These effects last 24 hours, until the next daily preparations, or until another meal is consumed.
TraitDescription.Meditation: A spell with the Meditation trait means that you must have Zeal to Sustain it. Typically, casting a Meditation spell grants you Zeal, and they grant a series of actions you can take when you Cast or Sustain the spell, called Recitations. If you lose your Zeal, the spell immediately ends.
TraitDescription.Music: Items with the music trait are services, repositories or sheets that either play or provide guidance on how to play music (or both). Music serves to appeal to or evoke emotions, and could provide benefits during social situations. Depending on context and description of the music and situations it is played in, it can provide circumstance bonuses or penalties when played. Some Music items will provide guidance on when its bonuses apply, but the GM has final say if a song can affect a situation.
TraitDescription.Nascent: A weapon with the nascent trait has a magical tradition associated with it. A creature wielding this weapon can use their spell proficiency to make attacks with the weapon if they can cast spells of the matching tradition.
TraitDescription.Nightmare: A creature with the Nightmare trait hails from or the realm of Oblivion. They are comprised of the elements of the void and nonexistence, and actively drain the elements of creation to sustain themselves or risk fading to nonexistence.
TraitDescription.Order: Effects with the Order trait are tied to the universal concepts of axiom, determining fate, fortune, and misfortune. They often have stronger effects on anarchic creatures. Creatures with this trait are emblematic of axiomatic forces and often have weakness to chaos.
TraitDescription.Pinotr: A creature with this trait is a member of the pinotr ancestry. Humanoids who live on land but not too far from the water and capable of holding their breath for extended periods, they have a dependency on nature to provide, and rapidly expand wherever they settle.
TraitDescription.Resolve: An option with this trait indicates that it uses Resolve Points, typically available to Empty as they push themselves to the limit to perform superhuman feats.
TraitDescription.Ritual: A spell with this trait can be cast as a Ritual, using the Ritualized Spellcasting rules.
TraitDescription.Runic: An option with the runic trait pertains to runic magic or the runic language. Runes dictate commands that can create fantastical and great effects. Unlike a normal language, it isn’t one that can be easily spoken or used for communication, as one must use magic to speak or write it in a way that it becomes usable; it has very little linguistic properties otherwise. Due to its potential dangers, is typically outlawed in a majority of countries if a creature does not have the proper permissions.
TraitDescription.Sapien: A creature with this trait is a member of the sapien ancestry. These are resilient humanoids who could historically thrive in just about any climate and are naturally resistant to disease, and have spread all over Ardor. As diverse as they are plentiful, they share spaces with almost every ancestry in Ardor.
TraitDescription.Scepter: A scepter is a type of magical implement that a spellcaster can charge with a spell to be cast later more readily.
TraitDescription.Soulforged: Items with the soulforged trait are either weapons crafted in the primal plane imbued with astral essences, or weapons crafted in the astral plane imbued with primal essences, created through the process of soulforging. A soul is often a core component of this process, and is consumed in its creation. Soulforged weapons also frequently have the Unholy trait.
TraitDescription.Spellcrux: A weapon with the spellcrux trait can take on the powers of a charged staff, and act like a staff to cast spells from it. The weapon either has a spell list of its own like a staff would, or if not, a spellcaster charging a staff can transfer its powers to a spellcrux weapon, transferring all spells and charges for the day into it.
TraitDescription.Sygican: An item with the sygican trait denotes that it is an item with sygicatech circuitry, allowing it to perform magical effects while being used by those who do not have the ability to wield ether, such as Empty. As long as the piece of equipment has a fuel or energy source, such as a battery, a user of the item can activate its magical effects. In some sygicatech items, this takes the form of Engrams.
TraitDescription.Symbiosis: An option with the symbiosis trait indicates an action or activity that can align a chimerian’s twin souls to acting in tandem. If you meet the requirements listed by the action, your souls harmonize; this grants the chimerian the ability to cast an anima spell without expending a focus point. This benefit lasts for one minute or until it is used.
TraitDescription.Telluric: Effects with the Telluric trait are tied to the etheric forces of the primal planes. They often have stronger effects on astral creatures. Creatures with this trait are tied to the workings of the primal planes and often have weakness to astral.
TraitDescription.Therian: A creature with the Therian trait has their soul changed in some way than typical creatures of their kind. Ancestral therians are those whose souls have been shaped by strong spiritual or planar influences, while true therians are those whose souls are eroded due to the presence of another soul interfering with theirs.
TraitDescription.Union: A weapon with the union trait is a 1+-handed weapon that is a combination of two separate paired weapons. When wielded in both hands, it is considered as if you were dual wielding two separate weapons for the purposes of meeting requirements of feats and actions that require weapons in separate hands. As a single interact action, it can be separated into two identical one-handed weapons with the same damage types, properties and traits as the weapon except for this trait, and they both gain the Twin trait. When separated in this way, you choose which of the two halves gains the benefits of any runes inscribed on the weapon. If you wield both halves at once, the half you did not choose replicates any runes from the main half. The two halves can be recombined with another interact action.
TraitDescription.Vashlad: A creature with this trait is a member of the vashlad ancestry. These ancient humanoids hailing from the Schattenriss are made of tough, supernatural muscle and bone, and have numerous forms that are influenced by their lineage. Some bear wings, others bear fangs, mandibles or sharp ears, and more.
TraitDescription.Vesperan: A creature with this trait is a member of the vesperan ancestry. These magical, winged batlike humanoids originate from the machinations of the drachiri's experimentation built to combat the Avekiri, but they have since broken free and expanded across Ardor.
TraitDescription.Vehicle: An item with the Vehicle trait is a service or upgrade to an existing vehicle. These typically include in their stat block the vehicle or type of vehicle they apply to, and denote a benefit when applied to the vehicle.
TraitDescription.Zeal: Zeal is a resource that you gain from taking specific actions as a Dervish that you can spend for Zenith actions. When you take these actions in Encounter Mode, you gain one point of Zeal at the start of the action. If you have multiple sources that qualify for granting Zeal with an action, you gain one point for each source. You can have up to 5 points of Zeal at any one time, and you lose all Zeal at the end of the turn unless you gain Zeal during your turn or spend a single action with the Concentrate trait to maintain it. You lose all Zeal shortly after encounter mode ends.
TraitDescription.Zenith: Zenith actions spend all your Zeal. You must have at least one point of Zeal to use a Zenith action. You spend all your Zeal before you cause its effects; typically increasing in effectiveness with more Zeal spent. You do not gain Zeal during a Zenith action, even if it entails performing actions that would normally grant you Zeal.

Aid.Title: Aid
Aid.Text: When two characters are using the same skill, one of which to Aid the other, to achieve the same goal, you can use the higher outcome of the two checks to accomplish the goal at its intended DC while the lower of the two is used for the Aid check outcome. Both characters must meet all prerequisites and requirements, such as feats or proficiencies, and the nature of the Aid must be such that both characters are performing identical or combined tasks for its duration.

AvertGaze.Title: Avert Gaze
AvertGaze.Text: Avert Gaze: Avert Gaze is now a free action you can take at the start of your turn, which confers a +2 circumstance bonus to saves to persistent gaze effects as normal. In the case of instantaneous gaze effects, so long as you are averting your gaze at the time the effect triggers, you treat the degree of success of your saving throw as one step higher.

Craft.Title: Craft
Craft.Text: Crafting has seen substantial adjustments in the Seekers of Ardor ruleset, as seen here: @UUID[Compendium.immortal-ardor.journals.JournalEntry.rN7GRW2OrOZmmzr3.JournalEntryPage.9nt9G1C7mXGDCYVB]{Ardorean Crafting}. Crafting is made with 2 checks; the first to prepare and plan materials to set the time and difficulty of a project, and a second for creating the item in question.

Ready.Title: Ready
Ready.Text: Readying a non-Move free action or 1 action activity now only requires 1 action instead of 2 actions. You can also ready a 2 action activity with 2 actions, or a 1-action Move action with 2 actions. Depending on circumstances and the action you are readying, the trigger you designate can be freely changed.

Stride.Title: Stride
Stride.Text: Striding will allow a simple Interact action as part of the same action. Opening an easy to open door mid movement, fetching or passing an easy to take unattended item, etc. This Stride cannot be a subordinate action, such as a Stride as part of Sudden Charge, or a move action that is part of a movement with the Traversal trait. When Interacting like this, Stride gains the Manipulate trait.

CreateADiversion.Title: Create a Diversion
CreateADiversion.Text: You can declare to distract others away from you or towards you. If you declare to distract others towards you, an ally of your choice gains the benefits of a successful diversion instead. You don't need to be observing your ally or know where they are, but you need to know they're present to choose them, and the hidden condition lasts until the end of that ally's turn.

MakeAnImpression.Title: Make an Impression
MakeAnImpression.Text: Make an Impression allows you to target up to 5 targets without penalty if you are Trained. This becomes 20 targets if you are an expert, 50 if you're a master, and 100 if you're legendary. Beyond these listed numbers, you take a -2 penalty, and the penalty increases by an additional 2 for each multiple of these numbers.

Coerce.Title: Coerce
Coerce.Text: Coerce allows you to target up to 5 targets when you are trained. These numbers increase to 10 if you’re an Expert, 25 if you’re a Master, and 50 if you’re Legendary. Beyond these listed numbers, you take a -2 penalty to your attempts, and the penalty increases by an additional 2 for each multiple of these numbers.

Demoralize.Title: Demoralize
Demoralize.ReplacementText: Using your words or your physique, you can shake an enemy’s resolve. Choose a creature within 30 feet of you who you’re aware of. Attempt an Intimidation check against that target’s Will DC. If you use your words or shout, this action gains an Auditory trait. If you menace with your actions or looks, this action gains the Visual trait. When you become a Master in Intimidation, this range increases to 60 feet. Critical Success The target becomes frightened 2. Success The target becomes frightened 1.

Counterspell.Title: Counterspell
Counterspell.Text: In place of the usual requirements or triggers, you can use counterspell if you have identified the spell and have a qualifying spell and can cast it. A qualifying spell is a spell that is the same as the triggering spell or a spell that shares at least one of the triggering spell’s traits other than concentrate, manipulate or its tradition trait. If you use the same spell as the triggering spell, you suffer no penalty to the counteract check. If you use a different spell, you take a -2 circumstance penalty to the counteract check. For each additional qualifying trait that matches after the first, you reduce this penalty by 1.

QuickDraw.Title: Quick Draw
QuickDraw.Text: Your hands move quickly. You can either Interact twice to perform any combination of Drawing, Put Away, or Swap items in your hands, or Interact once to perform these actions and Strike with a weapon afterward. If you have multiple sets of hands, one of these Interact actions can be to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e-anachronism.actions.Item.oW81CfM9ebxXnrw3]{Switch Hands}.

LightningSwap.Title: Lightning Swap
LightningSwap.Text: You have practiced quickly switching between combat styles and the equipment needed for them. You Interact to stow any number of items in your hands, and draw up to two items into your hands. If you have multiple sets of hands, you can @UUID[Compendium.sf2e-anachronism.actions.Item.oW81CfM9ebxXnrw3]{Switch Hands} in place of drawing an item.

ImpeccableCrafting.Title: Impeccable Crafting
ImpeccableCrafting.Text: This feat applies only to the Crafting phase of Ardorean Crafting, not the Preparation and Planning Phase.

ImproviseTool.Title: Improvise Tool
ImproviseTool.Text: You can temporarily craft a jury-rigged tool from the list offered by spending 10 minutes and succeeding a Crafting check against the DC to craft them if you have the materials. These tools fall apart by the start of your next daily preparations.

RecognizeSpell.Title: Recognize Spell
RecognizeSpell.Text: Recognize Spell is a trained skill action for the magical skills. Classes that prepare their spells through a repository or collection can identify spells automatically if it is available in their list of prepared spells, even if they do not have those spells prepared.

Fortify.Title: Fortify
Fortify.Text: Fortify is a trained skill action for Crafting.

BonMot.Title: Bon Mot
BonMot.Text: Bon Mot is a trained skill action for Diplomacy.

Group Impression.Title: Group Impression
Group Impression.Text: Group Impression is unused as the revamped Make an Impression already includes its functionality.

GroupCoercion.Title: Group Coercion
GroupCoercion.Text: Group Coercion is unused as the revamped Coerce already includes its functionality.

IntimidatingGlare.Title: IntimidatingGlare
IntimidatingGlare.Text: Intimidating Glare is unused as Demoralize already includes its functionality.

Backswing.Title: Backswing
Backswing.Text: Attacking again after missing with this weapon grants you a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack rather than a +1.

Backstabber.Title: Backstabber
Backstabber.Text: Attacks against an off-guard creature deals precision damage equal to the number of weapon damage die, rather than 1 (or 2 if it is a +3 weapon).

Bomb.Title: Bomb
Bomb.Text: Alchemical Bombs function identically to how they are in Pathfinder, but their base range is 30 feet.

Grenade.Title: Grenade
Grenade.Text: Grenades function identically to how they work in Starfinder, but they are Martial weapons instead of Simple weapons.

Forceful.Title: Forceful
Forceful.Text: Subsequent attacks with a Forceful weapon adds a circumstance bonus to damage equal to 2 times the number of weapon damage die, rather than just equal to the number of weapon damage die.

Maneuver.Title: Disarm, Grapple, Shove, Trip
Maneuver.Text: As you can swap between 1-handedness or 2-handedness as a free action, these traits are adjusted so that attempts to use these actions with the weapon or unarmed attack with this trait allows the action to benefit from a target’s off-guard condition. @UUID[Compendium.immortal-ardor.equipment.Item.FgCLUHcWx97ZSbJU]{Effect: Maneuver Weapon}

Monk.Title: Forceful
Monk.Text: A Monk or anyone who has similar form of monastic training can use weapons with this trait in place of unarmed attacks for feats with the Monk trait or similar, assuming the weapon meets the requirements listed for the attack (such as needing a particular trait on an unarmed attack).

Sweep.Title: Sweep
Sweep.Text: Attacking another target with this weapon after the first on a turn grants a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack rather than a +1.

Twin.Title: Twin
Twin.Text: Attacks with the second weapon in the pair adds a circumstance bonus to damage equal to 2 times the weapon damage die rather than just equal to the weapon damage die.

DrachiriBenefactor.SecondBenefactorPrompt: As you have an existing Benefactor and took an option that might allow you to have another benefactor, choose to gain a new Benefactor or a new Trait.

Aetherfonts.EnforcerRefocusDescription: When Enforcers refocus, they usually practice physical or mental exertion for the approximate duration of Refocus in relation to their source of their focus points. Upon refocusing, they recover 1 focus point. If you select a feat that improves your Refocus, the first time you would gain a focus point after your last Refocus, you gain 2 focus points.
Aetherfonts.ReaverRefocusDescription: When Reavers refocus, they incorporate various deeds as part of their Refocus. Depending on circumstance, these may require skill checks. If they have ready access to any source for their focus points, they are free to perform other activities during the ten-minute period. At the end of the activity, they gain 1 focus point. If you select a feat that improves your Refocus, you can gain two additional focus points in the ten-minute period by doubling up on an activity or performing multiple activities.
Aetherfonts.InvokerRefocusDescription: When Invokers refocus, they spend ten minutes recovering their magical connection in an activity that is appropriate to their source of their focus spells or magic. These deeds can usually overlap with other tasks that relate to the source of your focus spells. For instance, a cleric can usually Refocus while tending the wounds of their allies, and a wizard might be able to Refocus while attempting to Identify Magic. At the end of this period, they recover 1 focus point and enter a state of @UUID[Compendium.immortal-ardor.feats.Item.4XSYk2WQYoTODUG4]{Clarity}. If you take a feat to improve your Refocus, you recover all your focus points within the ten-minute period.
Aetherfonts.InvokerConserveEtherDescription: Whenever you use your focus points, you can roll a @Check[flat|dc:16]check. On a success, you retain one focus point.
Aetherfonts.EvokerRefocusDescription: Evokers do not need to perform dedicated activities to Refocus as they take in ether naturally. As long as they do not perform any strenuous activity, they are able to perform any other Exploration activity as part of their Refocus. At the end of a ten-minute period of these light activities, they regain one focus point. If you take a feat that improves your Refocus, you can take up to two qualifying items you can use for Spell Catalyst and drain it during your Refocus. This acts as if the item had been used for Spell Catalyst, but you regain an additional focus point for each item you drain within the ten-minute period.
Aetherfonts.EvokerSpellCatalystDescription: You can use items and components that possess a suitable amount of ether to help charge your spell. To qualify, the consumable item must possess at least one trait that matches the spell being cast that is not concentrate, manipulate or a spell tradition trait, or the item interacts specifically with the spell. You negate 1 point of the focus point cost. This consumes, uses, or activates the item, whichever applies. If the item can be used as part of the spell, such as a qualifying catalyst for the spell it is made for, the spell still benefits from the catalyst’s effects.
Aetherfonts.EvokerSpellScavengerDescription: Improvising on the fly, you can use natural items or nearby terrain as a source of ether. You use the object or terrain to negate one point of the focus point cost of the triggering spell.
Aetherfonts.EmptyEmptyResiliencePrompt: Select a benefit for Empty Resilience.

MoltingSkinRemedy.EffectPrompt: Select your Molting Skin Remedy bonus, based on proficiency and check outcome

DraichsarBreath.BreathDescription: You reach into the well of magic within you and ignite the dracoleum within, launching a blast of energy through your maw. Your dragon breath deals @Damage[ceil(@actor.level/2)d{actor|flags.system.drachiriBenefactor.breathDieSize}[@actor.flags.pf2e.drachiriBenefactor.damageType]|options:area-damage]. Each creature in the area must attempt a @Check[type:{actor|flags.system.drachiriBenefactor.breathSave}|dc:resolve(@actor.system.attributes.classOrSpellDC.value)|basic:true] saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You can’t use this ability again for [[/r 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
DraichsarBreath.BreathSpecDescription: On a critical failure on a saving throw, you apply the breath weapon's critical weapon specialization effect to the creature. If your damage type is vitality or void, you add 2d6 persistent damage of that type on a critical failure.
DraichsarBreath.ConeDescription: Your breath takes the shape of a @Template[type:cone|distance:15].
DraichsarBreath.LineDescription: Your breath takes the shape of a @Template[type:line|distance:30].
DraichsarBreath.BurstDescription: Your breath takes the shape of a @Template[type:burst|distance:10].
DraichsarBreath.DeepConeDescription: Your breath takes the shape of a @Template[type:cone|distance:30].
DraichsarBreath.DeepLineDescription: Your breath takes the shape of a @Template[type:line|distance:60].
DraichsarBreath.DeepBurstDescription: Your breath takes the shape of a @Template[type:burst|distance:20].

PackBonuses.MarkOfThePackDescription:
You are adjacent to an ally. When you or the ally makes a successful Strike or spell attack against a creature, the other gains a circumstance bonus to their next Strike or spell attack against the same creature.

DragonsGreed.Label: Dragon's Greed
DragonsGreed.Description: Once per round, you @UUID[Compendium.immortal-ardor.macros.Macro.GKvebOKUsIBQZhbN]{Gain Zeal} when using actions with the Flourish trait, or when you Tumble Through, Maneuver in Flight or Fly.
